title: Qwen3-235B-A22B (Instruct)
name: Qwen3-235B-A22B (Instruct)
description: Qwen3-235B-A22B (Instruct) is the flagship sparse MoE production variant in the Qwen3 family, designed for hard reasoning, long-context chat, code, math, and complex tool-using agents with a strong emphasis on thinking/non-thinking control. It is operationally much heavier than dense mid-tier Qwen3 models, but its 235B total / 22B active design is the core deployment advantage when quality needs justify multi-GPU inference and MoE routing overhead. For production, the main decision is not whether it can run, but whether your serving stack, memory budget, and latency envelope can absorb a 128K-context MoE model with explicit reasoning behavior.

hardware.recommended_gpu: NVIDIA H100/H200-class or equivalent multi-GPU infrastructure

runtime_compatibility.notes: Official model card says Qwen3-MoE support is in latest Transformers and warns that versions below 4.51.0 can raise KeyError: 'qwen3_moe'.
Official model card explicitly recommends vLLM and gives a serving command with --enable-reasoning and --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1.
Official model card explicitly recommends SGLang and shows --reasoning-parser qwen3 plus tensor-parallel deployment.
Official release materials and downstream ecosystem guidance support local GGUF serving; exact minimum version is not specified.
Official release materials say Ollama support is available for local use.
Official release materials say LM Studio supports Qwen3 local use.
Official release materials mention MLX-LM support for local use.
Supported through deployment ecosystem guidance, but the official model card does not publish a minimum version.

deployment.recommended_quantization: BF16 for maximum fidelity if you can afford the memory footprint; AWQ or GPTQ for production cost reduction when you have validated that reasoning quality remains acceptable.

best_for: Hard reasoning workloads where quality matters enough to justify MoE serving cost.
Complex tool-using agents that benefit from native thinking mode and explicit reasoning parser support.
High-end chat and long-context enterprise deployments with 128K-class workflows.
avoid_for: Small single-GPU deployments where latency and memory are tight.
Teams that cannot operate multi-GPU MoE infrastructure or long-context KV-cache-heavy workloads.
Cases where a dense 7B–32B model already meets quality requirements at much lower cost.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Cluster-scale reasoning and agent serving with explicit thinking-mode control and long-context support.
deployment_risks: Underprovisioning memory for BF16 MoE serving. Plan for multi-GPU sharding from day one; treating it like a large dense checkpoint is a common failure mode in practice.
Enabling long-context scaling globally when most requests are short.
failure_modes: KeyError: 'qwen3_moe' when using a Transformers version older than 4.51.0.
Degraded short-text performance if YaRN is enabled unnecessarily.
common_mistakes: Using a Transformers version older than 4.51.0.
Treating Qwen3-235B-A22B like a large dense checkpoint rather than planning for multi-GPU sharding and MoE routing overhead.
operational_notes: The official model card recommends enable_thinking=True by default and documents separate thinking and non-thinking modes; for thinking mode, it recommends Temperature=0.6, TopP=0.95, TopK=20, MinP=0, and warns against greedy decoding because it can degrade quality and induce repetition.

The model card also recommends max_new_tokens=32768 for standard use and up to 38912 for especially hard math/programming benchmarks, which is a strong signal that output-length policy is part of the serving contract for this model.
MoE routing plus long-context KV cache makes this variant materially more sensitive to batching and memory policy than dense family members.

The official model card recommends vLLM and SGLang deployments, including explicit example commands with reasoning parsers; use those paths if you need production OpenAI-compatible serving with thinking-mode fidelity.
For long contexts, the official guidance recommends YaRN and notes that static YaRN can hurt shorter-text performance, so only enable it when the workload actually needs >32K context.
Use YaRN only when the application needs long-context inference; the model card warns that it can degrade short-text performance if enabled unnecessarily.
Use quantization only after task validation, because the model’s main value is reasoning quality and aggressive compression can reduce that advantage.
For serving efficiency, preserve the model’s separate thinking/non-thinking behavior rather than flattening it into one generic chat path.

Variant differentiation (Identity): the 235B/22B architecture places this model at the top of the family’s quality-cost curve, with deployment characteristics that are fundamentally closer to cluster-scale serving than to single-node inference.

Variant differentiation (Specifications): the 235B A22B instruct model is the only clearly documented Qwen3 text MoE checkpoint in the reviewed sources with 94 layers, 128 experts, 8 active experts, and GQA split of 64 Q / 4 KV, which makes it the most operationally distinct Qwen3 family member for large-scale reasoning deployment.

Variant differentiation (File Formats): unlike dense variants, this checkpoint is commonly served in BF16 plus quantized export forms, and those quantized paths are essential if you want to avoid full-cluster BF16 memory pressure.

Variant differentiation (Hardware Requirements): hardware is the defining difference for this variant — it is not a “big single GPU” model, and most deployment mistakes come from underestimating the memory needed for MoE routing plus 128K-context KV cache.

Variant differentiation (Downloads): use the Hugging Face model card as the canonical source for checkpoint-specific specs, and the Qwen official download portal when you need the family’s supported distribution paths and quantized artifacts.

Variant differentiation (Runtime Compatibility): this checkpoint’s documented runtime support is strongest in Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang; the model card also shows exact switching behavior for thinking mode, which matters more here than for smaller Qwen3 variants.

Variant differentiation (Deployment): the instruct MoE checkpoint is best treated as a service-tier model, not a local development model; the recommended deployment path is multi-GPU serving with explicit reasoning controls preserved end to end.
Variant differentiation (License): the license posture is straightforward and not the reason to choose or reject this variant; deployment feasibility is the real gating factor.
Variant differentiation (Status): the hosted service lifecycle is active, and the checkpoint remains positioned as a production-grade flagship MoE model rather than a research-only release.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-30B-A3B): Smaller MoE sibling with lower active-parameter cost and easier deployment footprint.
Variant relationship (Qwen3-32B): Dense large-model alternative with simpler serving characteristics but lower top-end reasoning capacity than the flagship MoE checkpoint.
Variant relationship (DeepSeek-R1): Alternative reasoning-first family for comparison when choosing a flagship reasoning model.
